item.title: Former US V-P Mike Pence says Ukraine is winning war
item.description: Former US Vice-President Mike Pence stated that Ukraine is winning its war against Russia, praising its military for reaching a stalemate and revolutionising drone tactics. He urged South Korea to ...
item.content:encoded:
Former US V-P Mike Pence says Ukraine is winning war Former US Vice-President Mike Pence stated that Ukraine is winning its war against Russia, praising its military for reaching a stalemate and revolutionising drone tactics. He urged South Korea to supply Patriot interceptors to ease shortages caused by US defence needs in the Middle East. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 11:11 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 11:11 IST

Former US Vice President Mike Pence (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Former US Vice-President Mike Pence said Ukrainian forces are gaining ground in their conflict with Russia, claiming that Kyiv's troops have held Russian forces to a stalemate while significantly reshaping the use of drones in modern warfare. Speaking to CNN from Ukraine after meeting President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday, Pence said Ukraine continues to show determination despite repeated deadly Russian attacks. "Ukraine is winning this war," Pence said. "Ukraine's military on the front lines has fought Russia to a stalemate." Pence was in Ukraine to attend a national prayer breakfast commemorating 35 years since the Soviet Union's dissolution and Ukraine's independence. The event was attended by thousands of people from Ukraine and international delegations, the former Vice-President noted. "The sense you have of the deep resolve, not only of the leadership from President Zelenskyy on down, but rank-and-file military, everyday Ukrainians, is palpable," Pence said. The former Vice-President said Ukraine had transformed the conduct of drone warfare, with its forces carrying out attacks within Russian territory and striking vessels in the Black Sea. His remarks came after a Russian "double-tap" attack killed at least 16 people and injured more than 100 others, CNN reported. The attack followed major Russian strikes on Kyiv. Pence said Russia had recently begun using high-arc ballistic missiles against targets in Ukraine. He said Ukraine was capable of intercepting drones but needed sophisticated interceptor systems to protect itself against ballistic missile attacks. Pence also warned that Russia could step up attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure as winter draws closer. "One of the things President Zelenskyy made clear to me is that he fully expects that, as winter approaches sooner than later, that Putin will start to strike not just children's schools and a hospital, as he did this week, not just a shopping mall, taking more than a dozen lives, but that he will start to strike that energy infrastructure," Pence said. According to CNN, military operations involving Iran have contributed to a shortage of Patriot interceptors globally. The US has used around half of its Patriot missile stockpile while defending against Iranian attacks, the network reported. Pence rejected the suggestion that Ukraine was suffering the consequences of President Donald Trump's war with Iran. "I don't see it that way, and I don't think the Ukrainians do either," he added. Pence said South Korea could help address the shortage of interceptors. He said Seoul has advanced interceptor systems that could be made available to the United States for use in the Middle East or Ukraine, or supplied to European allies. "This might be an opportunity for President Lee to step forward, make those interceptors available to the United States," Pence said. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after occupying and annexing Crimea in 2014. The conflict has since become Europe's largest armed conflict since the Second World War. Ukraine remains heavily dependent on Western countries, particularly the US and European allies, for weapons, ammunition and financial assistance. (ANI)

item.title: India's semiconductor market seen reaching USD 155 bn by CY31, share of global consumption to rise to 9 pc: Report
item.description: India's semiconductor market is projected to reach USD 155 billion by CY31, implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 20 per cent and taking the country's share of global semiconductor ...
item.content:encoded:
India's semiconductor market seen reaching USD 155 bn by CY31, share of global consumption to rise to 9 pc: Report India's semiconductor market is projected to reach USD 155 billion by CY31, implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 20 per cent and taking the country's share of global semiconductor consumption to roughly 9 per cent by 2031, according to a report by Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 10:53 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 10:53 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's semiconductor market is projected to reach USD 155 billion by CY31, implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 20 per cent and taking the country's share of global semiconductor consumption to roughly 9 per cent by 2031, according to a report by Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund. The report said India's semiconductor opportunity is being supported by a combination of domestic demand, a growing chip-design ecosystem, government support and the emergence of manufacturing and packaging capabilities. "India's semiconductor market to reach US$ 155bn by CY31E, a 20% CAGR that would increase India's share of global semiconductor consumption to roughly 9% by 2031E," the report said. According to the report's market trajectory, India's semiconductor market is estimated at USD 62 billion in CY26, with the country accounting for around 6 per cent of global semiconductor consumption. By CY31, the market is projected to rise to USD 155 billion, while its global share is expected to increase to 9 per cent. The report also highlighted the evolution of India's semiconductor value chain, with the country seeking to move from strengths in chip design towards fabrication, assembly, testing and related semiconductor infrastructure. As per the report, India's chip-design ecosystem is already a key strength. The country has around 3 lakh chip designers, accounting for about 20 per cent of the global chip-design workforce, with India ranked second only to the United States. The report said India's current position in chip design is "Strong", while its CY30 ambition is "Leadership". In wafer fabrication, the current position is described as "Absent", with the target of reaching "Pilot-Scale". Similarly, OSAT/ATMP is currently "Emerging" and targeted to become "Scaled" by CY30. The report identified several enablers for this transition, including the Chip-to-Startup (C2S) programme, Design Linked Incentive (DLI), Global Capability Centres (GCCs), semiconductor projects and government support. It noted that Tata-PSMC's Dholera 28nm fab and projects involving Micron, Tata, Kaynes and CG Semi are expected to strengthen India's semiconductor manufacturing and packaging ecosystem. India's cost competitiveness in semiconductor assembly and testing is another potential advantage. The report said OSAT costs in India are estimated to be 20-30 per cent lower than peers, while the country's competitive advantages include cost and scale, a large talent pool and government support, including 50 per cent capex support. The report also projected a significant ramp-up in India's OSAT/ATMP capacity. Target capacity across projects is shown rising from 15 million chips per day in CY26 to 48 million chips per day in CY28, with projects involving CG Semi, Kaynes Semicon, Tata OSAT and the HCL Group-Foxconn joint venture. The report further pointed to strong end-market demand as a critical driver for the semiconductor ecosystem, with 5G, electric vehicles, defence and AI data centres identified as key demand generators. It estimates India's CY30 semiconductor end-market at around USD 103 billion. However, the report also highlighted India's dependence on imports across several semiconductor-related categories, including semiconductor equipment, specialty chemicals, electronic-grade gases, silicon wafers, substrates/lead frames and other inputs. The report's projections indicate that India's semiconductor opportunity is expected to expand rapidly through the end of the decade, with rising domestic consumption, a large design talent base, increasing OSAT/ATMP capacity and investments in fabrication providing the foundation for a broader semiconductor value chain. (ANI)

item.title: 'We took the head off the snake': US to enter 'new phase' in Iran war very soon, says Speaker Mike Johnson
item.description: US House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that the war involving Iran will soon enter "a new phase" with expected allied support. Reaffirming confidence in Republican midterms despite economic pressures ...
item.content:encoded:
'We took the head off the snake': US to enter 'new phase' in Iran war very soon, says Speaker Mike Johnson US House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that the war involving Iran will soon enter "a new phase" with expected allied support. Reaffirming confidence in Republican midterms despite economic pressures like rising petrol prices, Johnson emphasised that President Donald Trump successfully prevented Iran from securing nuclear weapons capabilities. ANI | Updated: 24-08-2026 10:22 IST | Created: 24-08-2026 10:22 IST

US House speaker Mike Johnson (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The war in Iran is slated to transition into "a new phase" in the near future, according to Mike Johnson, the Speaker of the US House of Representatives, who noted his expectation that partner nations will provide support during this next stage. "I think we're going to get into a new phase here very soon. I believe our allied nations are going to assist in the next phase, and we'll get this finished," Johnson stated during an interview on Fox News on Sunday. He claimed that President Donald Trump successfully blocked Tehran from acquiring nuclear armaments, describing it as "a goal for all previous administrations". "We had to make sure the largest state sponsor of terrorism did not have a nuclear weapon. That was an objective of every administration for the last 50 years. Donald Trump did it," Johnson said, adding that commercial oil tankers were still navigating the Strait of Hormuz. He also cited deep-seated mistrust towards Tehran during diplomatic talks as a major hurdle. Johnson said, "You can't trust the Iranians on the other side of the negotiating table. That's the challenge." The House Speaker expressed strong confidence that the Republican Party will preserve its majority in the chamber, despite public pushback surrounding the ongoing military engagement in Iran. Asked by Fox News whether Republicans could win in the midterm elections in November if the conflict is still ongoing, Johnson said, "Absolutely". However, he added that "it would be helpful to get that thing resolved" before voters head to the polls on November 3. Johnson's statements come amid rising domestic frustration over the military campaign, which has driven up energy costs and spurred broader economic inflation across the United States, where petrol prices have climbed past USD 4 per gallon (3.8 litres) from under USD 3 prior to the conflict. The House Speaker, a prominent ally of President Trump, maintained that Republicans will succeed at the ballot box regardless of whether active combat ends by November. "People know we took the head off the snake," Johnson said of Iran. "We had to make sure the largest state sponsor of terrorism did not have a nuclear weapon." The Trump administration maintains that the military strikes against Iran were executed to prevent the nation from developing nuclear capability. Joint US and Israeli forces conducted military operations against Iran on February 28, resulting in the deaths of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei along with several senior government officials. Tehran responded by shutting down maritime access through the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial conduit for international fuel supplies, and launching drone and missile strikes directed at American military facilities throughout the Middle East. Following an initial ceasefire agreement reached in April, the region has experienced recurring flare-ups and intermittent military exchanges. Although active fighting has decreased in recent weeks, Trump announced "crushing" economic sanctions against Tehran, prompting global markets to prepare for widespread restrictions targeting Iran and its international trading partners. A precarious ceasefire remains in effect among the US, Israel, and Iran, though persistent friction continues to impact maritime security. The potential integration of allied military forces could signal a pivotal shift from diplomatic channels towards potential escalation. Iranian officials remain steadfast, declaring that the country will not relinquish control over the Strait of Hormuz, where transit disruptions have caused severe spikes in global fuel and natural gas prices. Johnson also highlighted reports of increased maritime oil traffic passing through the strategic waterway. "We're getting the job done step by step," the House speaker told Fox News. (ANI)
